items.followUp: A machine receives 500 J of energy and delivers 400 J of useful work. What is its efficiency?

rubric.why: States the defining efficiency of an ideal system.
rubric.description: An ideal system has 100% efficiency: its useful output work equals its input work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the efficiency as 100% and 1 mark for stating that output work equals input work (or that no energy is lost).

modelAnswer: An ideal system is 100% efficient.
In an ideal system, useful output work equals input work; no energy is lost.

items.followUp: What is a stopwatch? Explain how a digital stopwatch measures a time interval.

rubric.why: Gives the purpose of a stopwatch.
rubric.description: Defines a stopwatch as an instrument used to measure a time interval.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that it measures a time interval.

rubric.why: Describes the digital display and its controls.
rubric.description: A digital stopwatch has a digital display and start/stop controls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the display and start/stop operation.

rubric.why: Explains the electronic timing mechanism.
rubric.description: Its electronic circuit uses regular pulses from a quartz crystal oscillator to measure time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the quartz oscillator or regular electronic pulses and the counting circuit.

rubric.why: Includes the usual precision of the digital stopwatch described in the textbook.
rubric.description: It can measure time intervals to 0.01 s (one-hundredth of a second).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the precision as 0.01 s or 1/100 s.

modelAnswer: A stopwatch is an instrument used to measure a time interval.
A digital stopwatch has a digital display and start/stop and reset buttons.
A quartz crystal oscillator produces regular pulses, which an electronic circuit counts to measure time.
The time interval is shown on the display, usually to the nearest 0.01 s.

items.followUp: Using a velocity-time graph, derive the equation v² = u² + 2as.

rubric.why: Uses the area under the velocity-time graph to obtain displacement.
rubric.description: The area of the trapezium under the graph gives s = ½(u + v)t.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining displacement from the graph as the trapezium's area.

rubric.why: Uses the graph's slope to express acceleration.
rubric.description: The slope gives a = (v − u)/t, so t = (v − u)/a.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the acceleration relation or its rearrangement for t.

rubric.why: Correctly substitutes the time relation into the displacement expression.
rubric.description: Substitution gives 2as = (u + v)(v − u).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution or equivalent intermediate equation.

rubric.why: Reaches the required third equation of motion.
rubric.description: Simplifies to v² = u² + 2as.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: For a velocity-time graph, the displacement is the area under the graph.
The area of the trapezium is s = ½(u + v)t.
The slope of the graph gives acceleration: a = (v − u)/t.
Therefore, t = (v − u)/a.
Substituting in the displacement equation: s = ½(u + v)(v − u)/a.
Thus, 2as = (u + v)(v − u) = v² − u².
Therefore, v² = u² + 2as.

items.followUp: A room measures 8 m × 5 m × 4 m. If the density of air is 1.2 kg m⁻³, find the mass of air in the room.

rubric.why: Records the room dimensions in SI units.
rubric.description: Given dimensions are 10 m, 7 m and 6 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the room dimensions in metres.

rubric.why: Selects the volume relation for the rectangular room.
rubric.description: Uses V = length × width × height.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct volume formula.

rubric.why: Calculates the room's volume correctly.
rubric.description: Calculates V = 10 × 7 × 6 = 420 m³.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct volume with unit.

rubric.why: Uses the relation between mass, density and volume.
rubric.description: Uses m = ρV with density ρ = 1.3 kg m⁻³.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct mass relation and density.

rubric.why: Gives the correct mass and unit.
rubric.description: Finds the mass of air to be 546 kg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: ρ = 1.3 kg m⁻³, l = 10 m, b = 7 m, h = 6 m.
Volume: V = lbh.
Formula: m = ρV.
Mass of air in the room = 546 kg.

items.followUp: Define centre of gravity and describe how to find the centre of gravity of an irregular cardboard shape.

rubric.why: Gives the definition of centre of gravity.
rubric.description: The centre of gravity is the point through which the whole weight of a body acts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the point through which the body's weight acts.

rubric.why: Describes the first suspension in the experimental method.
rubric.description: Make a small hole near the edge and suspend the lamina freely from it with a plumbline.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for suspending the lamina and using a plumbline.

rubric.why: Identifies the first vertical line used to locate the centre.
rubric.description: Draw a line along the plumbline on the lamina.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for drawing or marking the vertical line.

rubric.why: Completes the method and locates the centre of gravity.
rubric.description: Repeat the suspension from another point; the vertical lines intersect at the centre of gravity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for repeating the procedure and identifying the intersection.

modelAnswer: The centre of gravity of a body is the point through which its whole weight acts.
Make a small hole near the edge of the irregular lamina and suspend it freely from a pin.
Hang a plumbline from the same pin and draw the vertical line along the plumbline on the lamina.
Suspend the lamina from a second hole and draw a second vertical line using the plumbline.
The intersection of the two vertical lines is the centre of gravity of the lamina.

items.followUp: Describe how you would measure the time taken by a pendulum to complete 20 oscillations using a stopwatch.

rubric.why: Describes starting the timing when the event begins.
rubric.description: Press the start button when the event begins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for starting the stopwatch at the beginning of the time interval.

rubric.why: Describes stopping and reading the elapsed time.
rubric.description: Press stop when the event ends and read the displayed time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stopping the stopwatch at the end and reading its display.

modelAnswer: Press the start button when the event whose duration is being measured begins.
Press the stop button when the event ends and read the time shown on the stopwatch.

items.followUp: A body of mass 3 kg moves with a velocity of 4 m s⁻¹. Find its momentum.

rubric.why: Defines momentum using mass and velocity.
rubric.description: Momentum is the product of a body's mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or formula p = mv.

rubric.why: Gives the SI unit of momentum.
rubric.description: The SI unit of momentum is kg m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass and velocity of a body: p = mv.
Its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹.

items.followUp: State whether each quantity is scalar or vector: distance, displacement, speed and velocity.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining feature of a scalar quantity.
rubric.description: A scalar quantity has magnitude only.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a scalar has magnitude but no direction.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining features of a vector quantity.
rubric.description: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a vector has magnitude and direction.

modelAnswer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only, such as mass or time.
A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction, such as force or velocity.
